comment: Machine-readable feed list. Human rationale is in docs/risk_model.md.

feeds.why: Distribution hostnames currently marked online, derived from abuse.ch URLhaus. Small, security-only, not an adblock list.
Don't Route Or Peer netblocks. High-confidence, prefix-sized, meant for network gear. Good egress drop list.
Current Feodo/Dridex-family IPs. Tiny. Skip if empty or stale.

Phishing hostnames aggregated from PhishTank, OpenPhish and others, deduplicated against common allowlists. This is what the house segment loses when the AP's DPI engine goes; the agent segment gets it for free. Non-commercial license (CC BY-NC): fine for personal and home use.

Ads, trackers, telemetry and some badware, the 'hand brush' tier with few false positives. House segment only: bedtime Instagram and ad blocking are family policy, not a blocklist feed, and never touch the agent. Wildcard entries; dnsmasq address= blocks subdomains anyway.

DoH, VPN, Tor and proxy services a device could use to go around the house resolver. House only, and served only while HOUSE_BLOCK_VPN is on (role vpn): the ruleset drops WireGuard and OpenVPN themselves, this stops a VPN app from reaching its provider to sign in or fetch servers. Carries dns.controld.com; a HOUSE_PRIVATE_DNS endpoint still resolves, the more specific name wins. Also carries tailscale.com and Cloudflare WARP.

eyeball.comment: The table of eyeball networks (home broadband and mobile) for the eyeball check of the broker (docs/fence.md, eyeball_network). An ASN is in the table when an asns feed includes it and none excludes it. user_agent is the User-Agent of each feed of this section: iptoasn.com, bgp.tools and PeeringDB. bgp.tools asks for a contact in it. A contact that you put in user_agent goes to all these publishers, not only to bgp.tools.

ranges.why: Each announced IPv4 range and its origin ASN, from the BGP table. Public domain, updated hourly.

asns.license: bgp.tools terms (fetch with a User-Agent, at most every 30 minutes)
asns.why: The class of each ASN. Eyeball includes; Content excludes, so a host of servers that another feed calls an ISP stays out.

PeeringDB AUP (no bulk redistribution; each box fetches its own copy)
asns.why: Networks that call themselves Cable/DSL/ISP. Many large incumbents call themselves NSP, so this feed adds to bgp.tools and does not replace it.
